articles.title: Aedes aegypti: cerca de 1,8 mil cidades estão em alerta ou em situação de risco por causa do mosquito transmissor da dengue | G1
articles.standfirst: A previsão de um verão mais quente e com chuvas mais fortes em 2026, por causa do fenômeno El Niño, aumenta a preocupação com a proliferação do mosquito - que também transmite chikungunya e zika.
articles.summary: A previsão de um verão mais quente e com chuvas mais fortes em 2026, por causa do fenômeno El Niño, aumenta a preocupação com a proliferação do mosquito - que também transmite chikungunya e zika.
articles.body:
Cerca de 1,8 mil cidades brasileiras estão em alerta ou em situação de risco por causa do Aedes aegypti . E a maior parte dos focos do mosquito está exatamente onde é mais fácil combatê-lo: dentro de casa.

O empresário Joel Silva fiscaliza reservatórios de água nos telhados da vizinhança e recebe vídeos de outros moradores de Botafogo, na Zona Sul do Rio:

“A associação é acionada, consegue falar com a prefeitura e a prefeitura toma providências”, conta.

Em Pernambuco, o número de casos de dengue está quase 30% maior do que em 2025, e já foram registradas seis mortes pela doença. A maior parte dos focos de Aedes aegypti está em vasos, pratos de plantas e outros recipientes que acumulam água.

“Até a água do gato eu troco. Todos os dias eu troco, com medo de entrar um bichinho”, conta a aposentada Luzia Maria Pinto.

Um levantamento do Ministério da Saúde mostra que cerca de 1,8 mil cidades estão em situação de alerta ou risco para a presença do Aedes aegypti, o mosquito transmissor da dengue, da chikungunya e da zika.

“Esse levantamento mostra que, em aproximadamente 50% das casas onde ele foi feito, foram encontradas larvas de Aedes aegypti”, diz Rafaela Vieira Bruno, chefe do Laboratório de Biologia Molecular de Insetos do Instituto Oswaldo Cruz (IOC/ Fiocruz ).

Aedes aegypti: cerca de 1,8 mil cidades brasileiras estão em alerta ou em situação de risco por causa do mosquito transmissor da dengue — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

No Laboratório de Biologia Molecular de Insetos da Fiocruz, a gente aprende a identificar o Aedes aegypti. Diferentemente do pernilongo, a gente não consegue ouvir o zumbido do mosquito. Outro detalhe é que a patinha dele é listrada e dá para perceber a olho nu. Professora Rafaela, que mais? Como a gente pode identificar em casa?

“A larva do Aedes aegypti tem medo da luz. Então, se você apontar um foco de luz e vir que elas se afastam, as larvas são de Aedes aegypti”, explica Rafaela Vieira Bruno.

A recomendação é limpar os recipientes pelo menos uma vez por semana.

“Jogar aquela água que está ali em um ambiente seco, jogar no solo, jogar na grama, no cimento. Nunca no ralo, nunca no vaso. Então, só jogar a água fora não é suficiente. A gente precisa limpar esse recipiente para ter certeza que a gente eliminou os ovos”, afirma Rafaela Vieira Bruno.

Em todo o Brasil, os casos suspeitos e confirmados de dengue tiveram uma queda aproximada de 70% na comparação com o mesmo período de 2025. Mas a previsão de um verão mais quente e com chuvas mais fortes em 2026, por causa do fenômeno El Niño, aumenta a preocupação com a proliferação do mosquito.

“É preciso estar atento, porque a combinação de altas temperaturas e chuva é excelente para o desenvolvimento do mosquito. É tudo de que ele gosta. A prevenção aos mosquitos é uma questão coletiva. É um dever de todos nós”, diz Rafaela Vieira Bruno.

articles.title: Mortes no trânsito da cidade de SP aumentam, e motociclistas são quase metade das vítimas | G1
articles.standfirst: Capital paulista registrou 782 mortes no trânsito entre janeiro e setembro de 2026; especialistas apontam imprudência e falta de fiscalização entre os fatores que contribuem para a alta.
articles.summary: Capital paulista registrou 782 mortes no trânsito entre janeiro e setembro de 2026; especialistas apontam imprudência e falta de fiscalização entre os fatores que contribuem para a alta.
articles.body:
O número de mortes no trânsito aumentou na cidade de São Paulo em 2026, com motociclistas entre as principais vítimas. Entre janeiro e setembro deste ano, 782 pessoas morreram em acidentes de trânsito na capital, contra 770 no mesmo período de 2025, uma alta de 1,5%.

Quase metade das vítimas deste ano estava em motocicletas: 48% do total. No período, mais de 370 motociclistas morreram, enquanto quase 300 pessoas foram vítimas de atropelamentos, segundo dados do Infosiga, sistema do Departamento Estadual de Trânsito (Detran).

A alta das mortes de motociclistas é uma tendência que vem se acentuando nos últimos anos. De 2017 para cá, o número de óbitos desse grupo cresceu 74% , apesar da criação da Faixa Azul, em 2022, iniciativa voltada à circulação de motos.

Para especialistas em mobilidade urbana, o aumento da frota de motocicletas ajuda a explicar o cenário, mas não é o único fator. As condições das vias, o comportamento dos condutores e a fiscalização também influenciam a segurança no trânsito.

“Eles não têm uma carcaça metálica em volta do corpo e conseguem desenvolver uma velocidade muito alta. Essa combinação de velocidade alta com essa falta de proteção sempre vai deixá-los mais vulneráveis”, afirma Ana Carolina Nunes, especialista em mobilidade urbana.

O aumento da frota de motocicletas na capital acompanha a tendência de crescimento das mortes. Em 2026, a cidade já tinha cerca de 1,17 milhão de motos em circulação.

No entanto, especialistas destacam que a quantidade de veículos não explica sozinha o avanço dos óbitos. Infrações cometidas pelos condutores, como avançar o sinal vermelho e circular em corredores de ônibus ou ciclovias, também representam riscos.

A especialista Ana Carolina Nunes afirma que medidas de infraestrutura, como a Faixa Azul, precisam ser acompanhadas de fiscalização para produzir resultados na segurança viária.

“Mesmo ações de estrutura, como a própria Faixa Azul, elas não fazem diferença se não tiver essa fiscalização junto”, diz.

Ela também aponta que a velocidade dos veículos pode influenciar o comportamento de outros motociclistas. “Não dá para esperar que eles vão seguir a velocidade que está regulamentada sem essa fiscalização. Até porque, muitas vezes, o fato de um estar acelerando faz com que outro se sinta compelido a acelerar também, porque é um corredor”, afirma.

O diretor da FGV Transportes, Marcus Quintella, também relaciona a imprudência à falta de punição. “A imprudência é vinculada à impunidade”, afirma.

Para ele, os radares são importantes para coibir infrações, mas precisam ser capazes de detectar motocicletas. Quintella avalia que o problema é crônico e exige medidas para reduzir as mortes.

Apesar de São Paulo ter o dobro de ruas e avenidas do Rio de Janeiro, a capital paulista tem menos radares de fiscalização: são 879 em São Paulo, contra 1.042 no Rio.

Enquanto as mortes de motociclistas aumentaram, o número de equipamentos de fiscalização variou pouco na última década e chegou a cair entre 2017 e 2026.

Quintella defende que a fiscalização seja eficaz para combater as infrações e reduzir os riscos no trânsito.

“Os radares são fundamentais, mas têm que ser eficazes. Eles têm que realmente detectar a moto”, afirma.

A Prefeitura de São Paulo afirmou que trabalha continuamente para ampliar a segurança no trânsito, com campanhas permanentes de conscientização.

Sobre a Faixa Azul, a administração municipal disse que a iniciativa reduziu em 26% a gravidade dos acidentes com motocicletas.

Em relação aos radares, a prefeitura informou que uma equipe técnica avalia a necessidade de instalação dos equipamentos. A Companhia de Engenharia de Tráfego (CET) também realiza diariamente ações de fiscalização com equipes nas ruas.

Trânsito de veículos é registrado na região do Ibirapuera, no Corredor Norte-Sul, em São Paulo, em 16/10 — Foto: ANGÉLICA ALVES/FOTOARENA/FOTOARENA/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

articles.title: Avião que fez pouso de emergência é transportado em rio no Acre; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Aeronave foi parar no Rio Purus durante uma emergência no sábado (17). Moradores registraram passagem do aparelho pelo Parque Chandless puxado por uma embarcação.
articles.summary: Aeronave foi parar no Rio Purus durante uma emergência no sábado (17). Moradores registraram passagem do aparelho pelo Parque Chandless puxado por uma embarcação.
articles.body:
O avião de pequeno porte que fez um pouso de emergência no Rio Purus , em Santa Rosa do Purus , no interior do Acre, está sendo resgatado após a emergência ocorrida no sábado (17). Moradores do Parque Chandless, em Manoel Urbano , registraram a passagem da aeronave pelo rio de mesmo nome puxada por uma embarcação.

O g1 não conseguiu localizar os responsáveis pela aeronave desde o pouso forçado. Conforme integrantes da comunidade à Rede Amazônica Acre, moradores de terras indígenas da localidade ajudaram na retirada do aparelho do fundo do rio para que a operação seguisse viagem.

Ainda de acordo com os moradores, o veículo seria levado a Manoel Urbano.

A aeronave é utilizada em uma operação independente na região, que não tem ligação por terra com o restante do estado. O avião estava em situação normal, mas não possui autorização para táxi aéreo.

Avião que fez pouso forçado no Rio Purus foi transportada por barco até Manoel Urbano — Foto: Reprodução

O apresentador Marcos Bergson, que estava no voo, informou que o avião teve vazamento de óleo e uma pane no motor, e planou por cerca de quatro minutos até encontrar o rio para o pouso forçado. Ainda segundo ele, o piloto Douglas Campos teve fraturas nas costelas e deslocou um ombro.

"Estávamos retornando para Manoel Urbano, 15 minutos após a decolagem, o motor começou a apresentar falha. Não dava tempo de voltar e tivemos que pousar no rio", informou.

Bergson e o cinegrafista Jean Andrade foram a Santa Rosa do Purus para uma gravação e, de Manoel Urbano, retornariam à capital Rio Branco de carro. Além deles e do piloto, a enfermeira Tiffany Lustanares estava no avião.

Os ocupantes foram levados à capital ainda no sábado por uma aeronave do Centro Integrado de Operações Aéreas (Ciopaer). O piloto foi encaminhado ao Pronto-Socorro de Rio Branco para exames.

Testemunhas filmaram avião afundando no rio após o pouso forçado, todos os 4 ocupantes sobreviveram — Foto: Reprodução

Ainda de dentro do rio, o piloto Douglas Campos fez um vídeo no qual relatou a pane sofrida pelo avião. Conforme o comandante, a aeronave teve perda do motor a 3,5 mil pés, o que equivale a mais de 1.066 metros.

"Nós fizemos o que deu, perdemos o motor 3,5 mil pés em cima da nuvem, teto fechado, mas deve estar com teto aí 800, mil pés. Até a hora que consegui ter o visual com o solo, nós estávamos ali nos mil pés, pouco tempo para achar um local para pouso, viemos para o rio", explicou.

No momento do registro, os ocupantes ainda aguardavam resgate e o piloto disse ter ouvido o som de um motor de barco.

"Graças a Deus, todo mundo vivo, tivemos a perda financeira, bagagem, pouca coisa, nada comparado com todo mundo que está dentro", avaliou.

articles.title: Allyson faz campanha em Mossoró e propõe isenção de IPVA para motos | G1
articles.standfirst: O político do União Brasil caminhou com eleitores no fim da tarde desta terça-feira. Entre as medidas defendidas estão o perdão de dívidas de veículos e a redução de impostos na economia.
articles.summary: O político do União Brasil caminhou com eleitores no fim da tarde desta terça-feira. Entre as medidas defendidas estão o perdão de dívidas de veículos e a redução de impostos na economia.
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo do estado pelo União Brasil, Allyson Bezerra, realizou uma caminhada com moradores do bairro Aeroporto Dois, em Mossoró, no fim da tarde desta terça-feira (20). Durante o ato de campanha, o político conversou com a população, ouviu demandas e apresentou propostas.

O candidato estava acompanhado da esposa, Cinthia Bezerra, eleita deputada estadual pelo mesmo partido.

Entre as medidas citadas por Allyson estão a isenção do IPVA para motocicletas de até 179 cilindradas e o perdão das dívidas de motos apreendidas. Segundo o candidato, as duas ações seriam adotadas caso ele seja eleito governador.

"Nós estamos aqui apresentando o nosso projeto que é de zerar o IPVA para motos de até 170 cilindradas. Será uma importante medida que vai beneficiar dezenas de milhares de potiguares que usam a moto como o único instrumento de locomoção, de transporte, para trabalhar, aquele que usa para o seu pequeno comércio, que usa para ser entregador, motoboy", disse Allyson.

Ele também defendeu a redução de impostos no estado. O objetivo, de acordo com o candidato, é fazer com que mais dinheiro fique com a população e circule na economia. "Nós queremos destravar e focar na diminuição de impostos e de taxas. É comprovado que quanto mais você força o cidadão a pagar impostos, a pagar taxas, menos você está movimentando a economia", afirmou o candidato.

Outra proposta retomada por Allyson foi dar celeridade às liberações de licenças ambientais para o setor de infraestrutura. A medida envolveria o Instituto de Desenvolvimento Sustentável e Meio Ambiente do Rio Grande do Norte (Idema).

articles.body: HAVANA: Mining company Sherritt, which halted operations in Cuba over US sanctions, on Tuesday said Washington was allowing it to send fuel and other materials needed for nickel extraction to the island.The Canadian firm has mined nickel and cobalt in a joint venture with Cuba's state-owned General Nickel Company S.A. since the 1990s.Tuesday's announcement aims to allow a future resumption of its activities at the Moa mine after US sanctions pushed it to withdraw from the country in early May.Soon afer its withdrawal, however, Sherritt reversed the decision to liquidate its assets and said it was negotiating the sale of 55 percent of its shares with Gillon Capital -- a deal that would make the US firm Sherritt's majority shareholder.Gillon is owned by Ray Washburne, who served as president of the US government's development finance institution during President Donald Trump's first stint in the White House."The Fuel License" granted by the US Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) "authorizes the sale, transportation, export, delivery and payment for fuel, fuel oil, and sulfur to Moa Nickel, together with all related services," Sherritt stated.Talks with OFAC, the body that doles out Cuba sanctions, took place in close coordination with Gillon Capital, according to Tuesday's statement."The actual restart of operations at Moa Nickel remains subject to receipt of a second OFAC emergency license," it added.Washington imposed an energy blockade on Cuba in January, allowing only fuel shipments from the US and destined for the private sector to get through.Trump has openly mused about seizing control of the island, claiming that it poses a threat to US national security.(From news agency AFP)You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump commits more than $400m ahead of high-stakes midterm elections
articles.summary: The president’s Republican Party seeks to maintain its hold over both chambers of Congress, despite declining polls.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump has announced he plans to spend more than $400m to help Republican candidates win the November 3 midterm elections as his party fights to maintain its grip on Congress.

In a post on his Truth Social platform on Tuesday, Trump wrote that much of that total had already been spent on campaign outreach.

“More than 300 Million Dollars has already been spent on Advertising, Direct and Indirect Voter Contact, Rallies, Rally Arenas, Telerallies, Get Out the Vote Programs, Election Integrity, and more,” Trump said.

“It is my Great Honor to do so on behalf of the Republican Party, which has done so much to bring our Country back from the Edge of Oblivion.”

He added that the November vote was “the Most Important Midterm Elections in our Country’s History”.

The president offered no detailed breakdown of the spending, including how much would reach individual races.

But the promised influx of spending comes as Trump’s Republican Party faces headwinds ahead of the election, including pushback over the economy and the protracted US-Israeli war against Iran .

In the lead-up to the vote, Trump’s approval ratings have tumbled to record lows. A poll this week from the news agency Reuters and the research firm Ipsos found that only 31 percent of Americans approved of Trump’s job performance so far.

Some Republicans have sought to distance themselves from the president as a result. Others have pushed for greater support, particularly for close races with Democrats.

Questions have swirled over whether Trump and his allies would tap into the war chest amassed by MAGA Inc, the super PAC named for his “Make America Great Again” movement.

As a super PAC — or political action committee — MAGA Inc can raise unlimited sums from donors to support or oppose federal candidates. But its spending is legally required to remain independent of their campaigns.

Last month, the Campaign Legal Center (CLC), a campaign finance watchdog, accused Trump of violating those rules by claiming control over MAGA Inc’s expenditures.

The group cited the president’s public statements, including an exchange with reporters in the Oval Office on September 4, when Trump was asked when the money would start flowing to Republican candidates.

He replied that he would spend “whatever amount of money necessary” to help his party. He then added: “This is money from MAGA Inc. This is my money that I control.”

According to its latest federal filing, MAGA Inc entered September with $415.8m in cash reserves, making it one of the most consequential financial resources in the Republican campaign arsenal.

But Trump has questioned why the super PAC’s hefty outlay has not improved Republican polling in key races, including in Ohio, according to Reuters.

Other Trump-aligned groups have also ramped up their political advertising, including two newly formed organisations linked to MAGA Inc, the No Going Back PAC and the Safety and Affordability PAC.

The advertisement tracker AdImpact found that the No Going Back PAC contributed $68.7m in political ads last month alone.

Another Trump ally, tech entrepreneur Elon Musk, has reportedly spent $366m since last year on Republican campaigns through his group, America PAC, and other Republican and conservative groups.

In the final weeks of the midterms, Trump himself has hit the campaign trail, forging ahead with a 32-day campaign blitz . Upcoming stops include South Carolina and Iowa.

The stakes of this year’s election are considerable. Control of Congress hangs in the balance.

Currently, the Republican Party holds slim majorities in both legislative chambers, but Democrats are seeking to leverage Trump’s declining popularity to flip the Senate and the House of Representatives.

If they are successful, they could stymie Trump’s legislative agenda for the final two years of his presidency.

articles.title: Royals to visit Aberfan to mark 60 years since disaster
articles.summary: King Charles III, Queen Camilla and Prince William will join survivors and bereaved parents.
articles.body:
King Charles III, Queen Camilla and the Prince of Wales will be among the visitors to Aberfan on Wednesday to mark 60 years since the coal waste tip collapse in the former mining village that killed 144 children and adults.

A prayer and moment of silence will take place and a male voice choir formed after the disaster is set to perform.

The royals will also join survivors, bereaved parents and other members of the community to mark the anniversary, who will share their personal reflections.

On 21 October 1966, 116 children and 28 adults were killed when the colliery spoil tip collapsed and engulfed a primary school and surrounding houses.

The King, Queen and Prince William will visit the Aberfan Memorial Garden, built on the site of the destroyed Pantglas school, as well as the community centre where they will meet retired emergency service workers who helped in the response.

They will also look at an exhibition that shows the huge scale of the rescue effort, and spend time with former pupils at Pantglas school, siblings of those who died and members of the Aberfan Wives, a support group for mothers who lost children in the disaster.

The village's Ynysowen Male Voice Choir, formed in the aftermath of the disaster, also became a support group for local men to share their experiences.

Among those to speak are Jeff Edwards, who met the prime minister on Monday, and who was one of the last children to be brought out alive from the rubble.

Prince William will visit Ynysowen Community Primary School - which was established to carry forward the legacy of Pantglas Junior School - to unveil an Aberfan Memorial Tree.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham visited Aberfan on Monday and described the disaster as one of the "most horrifying tragedies this country has ever seen", adding it was something he was told about by his parents as he was growing up.

He addressed the issue of coal tip safety in Wales during his visit, saying it was of "critical importance" that the remaining tips in Wales are made safe.

Burnham met with survivors of the tragedy, including former Pantglas pupil Irene Hollett, who said the anniversary was a difficult time but that it was important for her to speak about what happened.

"A lot of stuff comes back to you. You feel grateful that you are still around 60 years on, but then you miss your friends and family that we lost at the time," she said.

"You can feel a bit of guilt that you are still here."

The royal visit comes after Queen Elizabeth II reportedly described her response to the Aberfan disaster as one of the biggest regrets of her 70-year reign.

While Prince Philip, Lord Snowdon and the then Prime Minister Harold Wilson visited the scene the following day, the Queen waited eight days before going to the village, arriving to comfort the community shortly after a mass funeral had taken place.

Years later the Queen's former private secretary, the late Lord Charteris, said he felt he had given her poor advice and that it was the biggest regret of her reign.

But she returned several times, and whenever she was in the area, her thoughts would turn to Aberfan.

In a personal message read to the community by the then Prince Charles on the disaster's 50th anniversary, the late queen spoke of a fondness for the people of Aberfan, saying she was "deeply impressed by the remarkable fortitude, dignity and indomitable spirit that characterises the people of this village and the surrounding valleys".

articles.title: Meet Raji Doshi, the 13-year-old from Farmington, Connecticut, who was named America’s Top Young Scientist and won $25,000 for a system that pairs seaweed with natural aragonite to reduce ocean acidification
articles.summary: Raji Doshi, who lives in Farmington, Connecticut, and attends Stanford Online High School, has won the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge, earning the
articles.body: Raji Doshi, who lives in Farmington, Connecticut, and attends Stanford Online High School, has won the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge, earning the title of America’s Top Young Scientist and a $25,000 cash prize. The announcement was made by 3M and Discovery Education on October 14, 2026.The eighth grader emerged as the winner after competing against nine other finalists at the final stages of the national middle school science competition, held at 3M’s global headquarters in St. Paul, Minnesota, on October 12 and 13.Doshi developed a system that combines macroalgae cultivation with natural aragonite, a form of calcium carbonate, to help address ocean acidification. Her project explores how the combination could increase the alkalinity of seawater, remove carbon dioxide and help protect marine ecosystems.How Raji Doshi’s algae-and-aragonite project tackles ocean acidificationTitled Engineering a Novel Durable Algae-Aragonite Alkalinity System to Reduce CO2-Driven Ocean Acidification, Doshi’s project investigates whether algae and natural calcium carbonate buffers can form a durable, low-cost solution to coastal acidification.According to 3M, Doshi used carbonate chemistry analysis to demonstrate how aragonite could increase algae biomass, remove carbon dioxide and substantially lower dissolved carbon dioxide levels. She also developed a Michaelis-Menten computational model to identify an optimal aragonite dose, with the aim of making the approach more practical for coastal communities.Her project, called ALKACORE, was inspired by her interest in collecting seashells and her concern about the effects of ocean acidification on shells and the marine creatures that depend on them.“Raji's project reminds us that when you're passionate about something, you can use that interest to change the world,” said Deborah Isabelle, a product engineering specialist at 3M who mentored Doshi during the competition.Isabelle added that Doshi was distressed to learn that ocean acidification was beginning to damage seashells and the creatures living inside them. That concern, she said, led the young scientist to develop her project.What 3M said about Raji Doshi’s achievementCongratulating Doshi, 3M Chairman and CEO William Brown highlighted the potential of young people to use science to address real-world challenges.“The 3M Young Scientist Challenge highlights the incredible potential of young people to tackle real-world challenges through science,” Brown said. He added that this year's finalists displayed exceptional talent and creativity.The competition pairs each finalist with a 3M scientist, who provides one-on-one mentorship over the summer to help transform an initial idea into a working prototype. Doshi worked with Isabelle as she developed her project.Discovery Education CEO Brian Shaw also praised the finalists for their dedication and imagination, noting that the partnership with 3M has spent 19 years connecting students with working scientists and helping them develop their ideas into prototypes.Who were the runners-up in the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge?The 2026 competition also recognised two runners-up, who each received a $1,000 prize.Aaisha Asif: A seventh grader from Pine View, Sarasota County Schools, in Sarasota, Florida.Sharvi Mahajan: A ninth grader at Westview High School in the Poway Unified School District in San Diego, California.The other finalists were Ahmed Abdelsalam of Cambridge, Massachusetts; Aiden Jo of Houston, Texas; Roy Kim of Beaverton, Oregon; Arika Kundu of Shorewood, Minnesota; Millie Pradawong of Fairfax, Virginia; Naboshree Santra of Oviedo, Florida; and Abigail Stein of Nashville, Tennessee.The finalists, aged 11 to 14, were assessed on creativity, scientific knowledge, communication, ingenuity, application of STEM principles and the quality of their research.About the 3M Young Scientist ChallengeNow in its 19th year, the 3M Young Scientist Challenge encourages middle school students to identify everyday problems and develop science-based solutions. Participants submit short videos presenting their ideas, with selected finalists receiving mentorship from 3M scientists as they refine their projects.The competition is part of a broader partnership between 3M and Discovery Education to encourage hands-on scientific learning. Its associated Young Scientist Lab programme offers free digital resources for students, teachers and families to explore science, technology, engineering and mathematics.According to the organisers, past winners and finalists have gone on to give TED Talks, file patents, establish nonprofits and appear on the Forbes 30 Under 30 list.You use AI every day. articles.title: 100 best travel essentials that make every trip better, tested and vetted by shopping experts
articles.summary: We rounded up the 100 most valuable travel products that make plane trips and car rides better, including packing cubes, compression socks, travel pillows and tech.
articles.body: Holiday travel has become quite the chore. Between high check-in fees, long security lines and middle seats that seem to only get tighter, you may find yourself feeling more stressed than excited about your next trip. To mitigate travel-related mishaps and to make your time en route to wherever you’re headed easier, the NBC Selected editorial team rounded up our 100 most essential travel products. As shopping editors, we’ve tried almost every major brand and random accessory you’ve heard good (or even so so) things about. We’ve tested neck pillows to find which ones are the most comfortable and pushed the limits of what a carry-on suitcase can actually fit, top-loaders included — all to find the most helpful tools that make travel, whether by plane, train or car, better. Bookmark this as you prepare for your holiday vacations and thank us later. Bon voyage. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Luggage & baggage Backpack are always my go-to for travel because they distribute the weight more evenly for my bad back than a tote. I recently treated myself to this one and am so glad I did. It looks sleek and polished but fits a ton inside. On a recent trip, I was able to pack my laptop, iPad, headphones, an oversized scarf, makeup bag and other odds and ends without it feeling like it was going to burst at the seams. - Bethany Heitman-Samuda, commerce editor Being an over-packer and someone who refuses to check luggage presents me with a challenge every time I go on a trip — I want to bring all my stuff, but I don’t want to use a large suitcase to fit it all. The solution to my problem? Halfday’s Carry-On Garment Roller. Not only is the main compartment deceivingly spacious, but it also has a built-in garment bag that folds out to fit long dresses and skirts, pants and suits. Plus, the wheeled duffel’s soft material lets me overstuff it and still close the zipper. There’s also interior shoe pockets, and lots of organization pockets that I put cords, socks and other small items in. The first time I flew with this bag, I wasn’t sure it would fit in the overhead compartment because I packed over five days’ worth of clothes inside and a pair of sneakers. But it slipped right in, and right then, I knew it would be my go-to carry-on for life. I love using it for roadtrips, too. - Zoe Malin, reporter I was gifted this carry-on eight years ago and it still zips like new. Sure, it has a few battle scars and scuffs, but it’s sturdy, glides effortlessly and has survived every single trip I’ve taken since. And, I always get compliments on the rose gold color. - Lauren Swanson, editorial director All eyes are on me when I roll into LGA (hopefully never JFK) with this beauty. It looks futuristic — and honestly, it is the future of travel luggage. The rectangular shape is a game-changer. It fits clothes and packing cubes perfectly without squashing them. No zippers means no snagging (a godsend if you’re constantly catching them on delicate fabrics), and the integrated lock system is intuitive and easy to set up. This bag is huge — but not oversized. Perfect for chronic over-packers like me. The material is sturdy, super easy to clean, and check-in stickers come off without a struggle. Plus, it glides like a dream through airports. - Jem Alabi, editorial operations associate This isn’t a brand I was familiar with but I suspect it’ll be on everyone’s radar soon. I took this suitcase on a trip to the Berkshires and it was able to handle the rocky terrain and the bumpy concrete of NYC. I love the leather handle, and the fact that it is aluminum making it the most sustainable luggage out there. The wheels are quiet and the TSA locks are built into the latch frame which makes it easy to close and secure. It also looks different from any other suitcase on the market so I don’t get confused at the airport. - Alabi More of our favorite luggage and baggage: Patagonia Black Hole Pack 32LLongchamp Expandable Le Pliage Original Travel BagSamsonite Carry-On Luggage Calpak Luka Expandable Laptop Tote Learn more: Away Luggage is Now Available on Amazon Cosmetic cases & dopp kits This toiletry bag is one of our tried-and-true travel accessories, and one I rarely leave on a trip without. It keeps my makeup, skin care and hair care products neatly organized and easy to access, especially given each of the four compartments is transparent, so I can see exactly what’s inside. I love that it’s soft-sided, which makes it easier to pack in an already over-stuffed suitcase. It even has a hook at the top to hang it from a door or mirror and avoid a mess of products everywhere. - Mili Godio, commerce editor I use these satin bags for my wigs when I’m traveling and for storage at home, but honestly, you could use themfor so much more. I’ve used one to transport shoes that had gems and precious accents. One could also work as a substitute satin pillowcase in a pinch, especially if you’re trying to catch some sleep on your flight. They’re especially important for keeping my wigs (my girls) from getting matted and knotty or shedding during transport, and they keep my big curly girls contained so that they don’t get cauch or snagged in any zippers. - Shalwah Evans, senior editor I’ve always brought a garbage bag on trips to use as a hamper. When I get home, the laundry room is my first stop, so this makes it easy to throw all my dirty clothes in the washing machine. A garbage bag hamper is certainly not glamorous, but I didn’t think I had any other options until I discovered the Stinky Bag. It’s basically a dry bag with an interior mesh pouch, and it comes in various sizes — I use the extra-large size for everyday clothes and the standard size for sweaty workout clothes. I stuff the bags with laundry throughout my trip, zip them up and pack them in my suitcase, and when I get home, I flip the bag inside out so the mesh pouch is exposed and throw the whole thing in the washing machine and dryer. My clothes come out perfectly clean inside the bag, making post-travel laundry less of a headache. - Malin My husband is infamous for “borrowing” cords when we visit family. So now, I bring this. It fits everything (chargers, adapters, mystery cables) and keeps them all right where I can see them. - Swanson I’m an overpacker through and through. I got these packing cubes a few years ago for a few weeks in Europe, and have been using them for every trip I’ve taken since. I’m able to fit at least 2 weeks’ worth of tops and bottoms in each cube — and that’s before compressing them. The compressed cubes fit perfectly in both a carry-on and a checked bag, with extra space for shoes and toiletries. The set also comes with a drawstring bag, which I like to use to store dirty laundry while I’m traveling. - Caitlin Cusack, associate social media editor More of our favorite cosmetic cases and dopp kits: Dagne Dover Hunter Neoprene Toiletry Bag Aer Dopp Kit L.L. Bean Personal Organizer Toiletry Bag Sea to Summit Clear Zip Pouch with Bottles Calpak Packing Cubes (Set of 5) Tech I bring a lot of electronics wherever I travel, but I try to compensate by minimizing the amount of charging gear I need. Ideally, I bring two charging bricks, a few cables and this wireless charging station. It can charge my iPhone, AirPods and Apple Watch at the same time, and charge them quickly too. And it’s tiny, it’s almost the same size as an Apple AirPods case. - Harry Rabinowitz, former reporter The first time I traveled abroad, I brought four plug adapters for four different countries. Luckily, I’ve since found this. When I went back to Europe, I bought this $20 universal travel adapter, which has virtually every plug you’ll ever need. It has four USB ports and one USB-C port, so I can charge my phone, Airpods, Apple Watch, and portable charger all at once. A dead device in a foreign country is probably my worst nightmare, so I’ll never travel without this universal adapter again. - Cusack I can’t sleep in silence. There needs to be some sort of noise filling the room, so I used to rely on a white noise app on my phone during my travels— it did the job, but I can’t say the audio quality was particularly notable. I discovered ErgoPouch’s mini noise machine while testing products for our Travel Awards in 2024 and I can’t believe how long I lived without it. It’s about the size of my palm and has a built-in loop you can hang it from, like on a bed frame, door knob or dresser knob. I use it for a few nights before plugging it in since the battery life is pretty impressive. One side of the noise machine is a speaker, while the other is a dim nightlight. I use the nightlight a lot more than I expected to, especially in dark hotel rooms. - Malin As a kid, my family never left for a vacation without bringing along my dad’s camera, and we have the photo albums to prove it. As an adult, I like to continue that tradition on my own trips; however, instead of a digital camera, I like to grab this Fujifilm disposable camera. Each camera has 27 shots, and I love that they’re easy to operate and small enough to stuff into my bag on my way out the door. The camera’s photos are also clear and well-lit, but have a slight grain to them that gives each photo a nostalgic touch. - Ashley Morris, associate reporter Learn more: What’s the deal with the $65 Camp Snap camera? After being a movie obsessive for so long, I decided that it was high time for me to start recording my own memories and experiences, which is why I got this camcorder before my last trip to Brazil. It has a long battery life and is easy enough for a beginner videographer like me to use with no issues. I also like that the videos have time and date stamps to help me keep track of the footage, and that the screen spins around for easier visibility while recording. - Morris This was finally the year I got sick of running on 5% battery or less. This powerbank isn’t fancy and it doesn’t charge up at lightning speed either, but once it does, I can charge my phone, laptop and headphones before it needs more juice again. It’s also slender enough to fit in the side pocket of my purse or luggage. The camera records HD 1080p video, and has a built-in microphone and night-vision mode for filming in the dark. You can also easily mount it on a tripod for steadier shooting, and capture photos in camera mode. - Nikki Brown, senior editor More of our favorite travel tech: Twelve South AirFly SE Sony WH-1000XM6 Noise-Canceling Wireless Headphones Apple AirTag Apple AirPods Max HeadphonesApple iPadApple AirPods Pro 2 Wireless Earbuds iWalk Small USB-C Portable Charger Kindle Paperwhite Hicober 3-in-1 Wireless Charging Station Health and wellness I first bought these during a rough round of antibiotics-induced nausea, and now I never travel without them. I’m naturally prone to nausea, whether it’s turbulence, motion, strong smells, or just a bumpy car ride. I usually pack Zofran, Dramamine, alcohol wipes, or essential oils, but these cuffs provide instant, reliable relief — especially when I don’t want to take anything orally. You wear them three finger-widths below the wrist joint, with the plastic stud pressing on your pressure point (near the thumb). They’re snug — on purpose — and you don’t have to keep them on for long to be effective. Last but not least, they come in a neat little carrying case. - Alabi I am unfortunately one of those people who’s not fun to be around if I don’t get a good night’s sleep. So when traveling can mean changes in time zones and sleeping in unfamiliar places, sleep aids are a priority. These travel packs of AdvilPM are a life saver, and I love that I can throw a few packs in my overstuffed travel bag instead of needing room for an entire bottle. I took these on my overnight flight to London, and I give them credit for how easily I got seven hours of sleep and beat jet lag. This comes with 50 packs, so it lasts me a while. - Kailey Sigoda, intern I don’t leave my house, let alone the state or country, with at least a few of these in my bag. My stomach is known to do strange things at any given moment, and the last thing I want is for it to start flip flopping while I’m at the Louvre. These tablets are chewable so I can take one anywhere without the need for water or a pour cup, and I don’t have to worry about TSA liquid regulations. And yes, they taste just as bad as the original liquid formula, and they work just as well (and quickly). - Evans I’ve never been the type to brush my teeth in airport bathrooms, but I do get a serious case of dry mouth — especially as a tea drinker and a fan of those addictive Maui onion pretzels on Southwest flights. I don’t like gum or traditional mints, so this spray has been a dream. It freshens breath, combats dry mouth, and has xylitol to help prevent cavities between brushings. I’ve noticed a difference in my oral health since using it regularly. I keep one in every bag — home, work, travel. The mint flavor is gentle (no burning), and it also comes in grape if you want to mix things up. It’s practical and makes me feel like a cool character from a teen drama. - Alabi Motion sickness is a common struggle for me; when I’m in a car, plane or boat, panic immediately sets in with the onset of nausea, dizziness and an upset stomach. Dramamine is one of the only treatments that actually works for me, and I have a tube in nearly every purse and backpack I own. I prefer the less drowsy version since the original formula makes me too sleepy, and it’s equally as effective, in my experience. I take one around half an hour before I’m in a moving vehicle for peace of mind. - Godio If you’ve ever had cramps while traveling, you know the struggle. I used to rely on boiling water in a traditional rubber bottle, which is obviously not feasible outside the house, especially on planes. Enter: the Slimpal. This little heating pad has truly saved me. A full charge delivers up to two hours of soothing heat. It has adjustable straps, so you can wear it under your clothes and move around hands-free. It’s discreet, effective, and easy to travel with. - Alabi These face wipes live in my gym bag, my desk drawer, and my carry-on — and for good reason. Whether I’m getting off a flight, leaving a workout, or just need to wipe the day off my face, they actually make me feel clean. No sticky residue, no overpowering scent. - Swanson I occasionally stop by Sephora to get more Touchland hand sanitizers whenever I run out. I love that they have such refreshing scents, but also are practical — they keep my hands clean without leaving a residue and they don’t have a strong alcohol aroma. Plus, they don’t dry out my hands, so I can use them more than once throughout the day, which I often do when I travel, especially by plane. - Cory Fernandez, commerce editor I know we’ve mostly moved on, but airplanes are still petri dishes with wings. I keep a few of these individually wrapped face masks in every bag when I travel. They’re comfortable, easy to breathe in and (most importantly) I haven’t come home with the dreaded post-flight cold since. - Swanson When I pitched our story on the best body wipes, I had chaotic travel days in mind — and these wipes deliver. Hand sanitizer and alcohol wipes are great, but for bathroom breaks, sweaty commutes, or quick freshen-ups, I need something gentler. Moonies are compact, durable, and actually flushable. I keep them on hand for everything from post-meal cleanups to rainy subway rides. They also make me feel like the most thoughtful friend when I offer one to someone else. - Alabi More of our favorite health and wellness essentials: Tylenol Extra Strength Rapid Release Gels Clorox Disinfectant Wipes Duracleanse Body Wipes Icy Hot Original Pain Relief Cream Lingito Travel Charcoal Toothbrush Food and snacks I used to think of hydration supplements as fancy juice, but after using them regularly, I see why people love them. They truly make a difference each time I drink them — I feel more refreshed and less tired in the morning, especially when I have to get up early for a flight. I also often get headaches after traveling, and these help me avoid that once I get off the plane. My favorite is the lemon-lime flavor, but there are so many options to choose from that you’ll definitely find one for you. - Fernandez I feel like a big kid when I’m eating one of these but honestly, I don’t care — I love them. I started buying these when I would go to the gym too early for me to have an appetite, but needed to put something in my stomach before a rigorous workout. Now, I travel with them too because they take up practically no space in my bag and I can eat them as I walk through an airport or ride in the back of a car. I also love that the cap can be screwed back on if I don’t finish it. The apple banana is my favorite; my friends with kids appreciate that I always have that flavor on hand when they come over because the kids love it too. - Evans More of our favorite food and snacks for travel: That’s it. Large Fruit Bars Variety PackEmerald 100-Calorie Snack Pack Orbit Sugar-Free Gum Good & Gather Trail Mix Accessories Every one of my co-workers has heard me rave about this handheld fan before — that’s how much I love it. It has an incredibly long battery life; I charge it once for an entire day and it lasts me for weeks. It has three speeds, and I rarely have to use the fastest one, since the first one is relatively strong. It also has a light on the end that I sometimes use when I’m looking for my keys or drop something in the dark. Plus, it’s the perfect size to fit in any pocket or cross body bag, which I do when I travel abroad. - Fernandez Learn more: This bladeless neck fan saves me from hot flashes After I saw a news report about a couple’s trip to the Bahamas ending in a carbon monoxide fatality I started taking this with me on vacation. It’s small enough to fit inside the bag that fits inside my personal item, which is where I keep it in order to ensure I have it no matter what happens to my luggage. It gives me peace of mind, especially since laws around carbon minoxide monitors differ by country (and even by state). I love that it also operates on batteries if the power goes out. Just be ready for the loud test ringing, the sound is piercing — exactly what I want if there’s an odorless, colorless threat present. - Evans I’m a light sleeper, so I’ve had plenty of hotel experiences ruined by loud street noises and conversations. Now, I take Loop’s Quiet 2 earplugs on every vacation. They’re lightweight and comfortable enough to wear all night long, and they manage to filter out enough noise for me to stay asleep through the night without filtering out too much noise (so I don’t feel like I’m in a soundproof cell). Plus, they come in a tiny case so I don’t lose them. - Godio I don’t take off most of the jewelry that I wear on a daily basis, and I never bring a bunch of accessories on trips, so I don’t need a large jewelry case taking up space in my suitcase. I do, however, need a safe place to put my rings when I’m working out, showering or doing a very hands-on activity. Enter the Lion Latch. It’s a little round, keychain-looking case that’s just the right size to fit all my stacking rings (eight, to be exact), and sometimes I throw in a dainty necklace or an earcuff. Each Lion Latch comes with a carabiner — I attach mine to a pouch or the key leash inside my bag if there is one. I also appreciate that it’s made from a hard, durable material, creating an outer shell of sorts around my jewelry so it doesn’t get scratched or nicked if I’m on the move. - Malin If there is one item I would recommend to anyone traveling abroad and staying in hostels — it’s this one. This microfiber travel towel will fit in any size bag, but is also big enough to use as a shower towel. When traveling during my semester abroad, we stayed in hostels nearly every weekend, and most don’t provide towels, or charge a fee for them. I relied on this. It comes in a compact storage bag, is very absorbent, and even has a loop on the corner, so you can hang it up to dry while you’re out sightseeing. - Sigoda My long hunt for spill-resistant travel containers ended once I found these bottles. Usually, I have to tape travel bottles shut to prevent them from leaking, but these are the only budget-friendly containers I’ve used that don’t create a mess of shampoo and face wash after being in my suitcase. The tops are extremely sturdy and never pop open during travel, and I love that the set of four comes with a zippered pouch to keep them together. - Godio As a lifelong overpacker, I always keep a luggage scale handy, and although I’ve tried plenty of digital scales, I always end up reverting to this manual scale from Samsonite. My old digital scales usually need periodic battery replacements, but since this one is manual, it’s always ready to go — it’s my favorite thing about it. It’s a bit bulkier than digital scales, but I’ve always found its measurements to be reality accurate, and I never leave for a trip without bringing it along. It registers up to 80 pounds, and has a handle grip that makes weighing my suitcases easy and comfortable. - Morris I’m a big fan of compressed packing cubes, which are great for saving space … but also great at wrinkling my clothes. Whenever I travel, I make sure to bring a bottle or two of Downy’s Wrinkle Release spray. All you have to do is mist it on your clothes, smooth out the wrinkles, and you’re good to go — no portable steamer needed. - Cusack More of our favorite travel accessories: Dagne Dover Frankie Jewelry CaseAspinal of London Passport Cover Cadence Pill Case SetHydro Flask Travel Water Bottle Large Print Word Search Books for Adults Pillows, eye masks and sleep essentials I was kind of unimpressed when I first saw this travel pillow because it looks more like a scarf. But after traveling through multiple time zones on a train in just one week, I’m glad this is the travel pillow I had by (and around) my side. Whether I was lying completely flat, sitting up with my head against the window or something in between, this pillow was able to shape shift into spaces and positions a boring neck pillow never could. - Brown I tested this eye mask for our Wellness Awards earlier this year, and I was surprised by how well it helped me fall asleep. Aside from making everything completely dark (which I love), it was extremely comfortable on my face. The “eyes” of the mask don’t sit flush against your eyelids — they’re raised, almost as if someone combined a pair of glasses with a pillow. Plus, the strap on the back is adjustable, so it was super comfortable on my head and didn’t give me a headache. - Fernandez As a very small person, my appreciation for this blanket knows no bounds. When I’m sitting in an airplane seat, it covers my entire body without grazing the floor or touching the person next to me. When combined with a hoodie, it provides the perfect amount of warmth. And I love that it’s easy to put in and out of the included storage pouch. - Brown I’ve had some version of this pillow for years. I don’t wear it around my head like a cartoon villain plotting on a red-eye, but I do wrap it around my neck or wedge it up against the window. It’s light, soft and folds down small enough to fit inside my personal item. - Swanson Learn more: You’re probably not cleaning your pillows correctly More of our favorite pillows and sleep accessories: Trtl Pillow Travelrest All-in-one Inflatable Neck & Body PillowKitsch Weighted Satin Sleep Mask Learn more: Do heatless curlers actually work? Skin care When I travel, makeup remover wipes are my go-to. But most come in large packs that take up more space than I’d like. I bought this pack of single, individually wrapped Neutrogena wipes that I can easily throw in my toiletry bag or backpack so I have the exact amount I need for my trips. Plus, I’ve always been a fan of these wipes — they take off stubborn makeup (including waterproof mascara) with minimal swipes, and they cause little to no irritation. And since each wipe is pre-wrapped, they never dry out. - Godio I don’t need fancy lip balm or body lotion: Vaseline does it all at a fraction of the price of most popular brands. I keep a small jar in my work bag, luggage and anywhere else I can think of. If I’m on an overnight flight or train ride, I like putting this on my face to keep my skin from drying out. I also apply to my lips every night before bed to keep them from cracking or peeling. And if I realize my elbows or knees are looking a little crusty as I’m moving through the airport, it’s much easier to apply some of this than a lotion that may end up exploding in my bag anyway. - Brown I tell everyone about this hypochlorous acid spray. I first heard about it from our former beauty reporter, and now I keep bottles everywhere — three at home, four at work, and one in my bag. Per my derm’s advice, I’ve stopped washing my face in the mornings (since I double-cleanse at night), and this Magic Molecule spray has been a total game-changer. It refreshes my skin, balances pH, and requires zero touching — so it’s a clean, hands-free experience. No residue, no stickiness: just a fresh, soothing mist. It’s helped calm my eczema, improved my skin texture, and even found a second life as a disinfectant for my beauty tools. I use it on everything: LED red light masks, Theraface, gua sha tools, eyelash curlers, edge brushes — you name it. - Alabi Between overzealous hand sanitizer use and airplane cabin air that could parch a plant, my hands are usually the first to suffer when I travel. This hand cream fixes that. It’s not fancy, but it works. - Swanson More of our favorite travel skin care: Biodance Bio Collagen Real Deep MaskCetaphil Gentle Cleansing and Makeup Face WipesDr. Loretta Urban Antioxidant Sunscreen SPF 40 Salt & Stone Hand Cream Gillette Venus Extra Smooth Travel Razor KitEltaMD UV Daily SPF 40 Tinted Face SunscreenBag Balm Original On-the-Go Lip Balm Tubes Supergoop Mini Glowscreen Sunscreen SPF 40 Learn more: This sheet mask is trending on TikTok and Amazon — is it worth it? Apparel and footwear These are the only compression socks I willingly wear — whether it’s after long runs or during long flights. The squeeze is subtle but effective, and they’re easy to put on and take off (which matters more than you’d think). I don’t wear them on every flight, but when I do, I’m always glad I did. - Swanson Everyone on the NBC Select team knows that I’m serious about my sneakers, so trust me when I say this: these are the best travel sneakers I’ve ever tried, hands down. They’re comfortable for long-term wear, and have enough grip on the bottom to get me through rainforest hikes, cobblestoned streets and more. They also don’t have traditional laces — these sneakers have a drawstring closure that you can tuck into the tongue, meaning you don’t have to worry about untied or loose laces. The bright color also adds a bold pop to any look, and the shoes have a sleek design that makes them feel lightweight on my feet, despite their durability. - Morris Slip-ons are a must for me when I’m traveling — I like to be able to easily get my shoes ff when I’m relaxing in my plane seat and on again for trips to the bathroom. These mules from Oofos are perfect. They have the most cushioned soles you’ll ever find, which makes treking through huge airports comfy and the sherpa gives them a stylish vibe. - Heitman-Samuda I wore these shoes through the airport on a recent trip, and I plan to keep wearing them. They’re breathable, soft, supportive and slip on in seconds, which still matters even if you’re not pulling them off for TSA. They’re comfortable enough to walk miles in (trust me, I have), sleek enough for a coffee meeting after. - Swanson More of our favorite apparel and footwear for travel: Uniqlo Wide Sweatpants Brooks Ghost Max 3 Running Shoes Uniqlo Sweat Oversized Pullover Hoodie Athleta Elation Ultra High Rise Straight Leg PantPrettyGarden Matching Loungewear SetBombas Ankle Socks Learn more: 50 best leggings of 2025, tested and ranked Pet essentials My dog Bella is 15 pounds, which means she can fly with me on a plane. The only problem? She hates most travel carriers. I’ve tried many over the years, but few have come close to the comfort and durability of this Away carrier. articles.title: Woman sexually assaulted at fraternity near University of Chicago, lawsuit alleges
articles.summary: The new allegations mark the second case of alleged sexual assault to roil the University of Chicago in a matter of days.
articles.body: A 19-year-old woman filed a lawsuit Monday alleging she was sexually assaulted at a fraternity house near the University of Chicago in February amid heightened scrutiny of sexual misconduct on college campuses. The college student, identified in court documents as Jane Doe, sued in Cook County Circuit Court, alleging that the sexual assault took place during a party at the Alpha Delta Phi fraternity house on Feb. 7. It names Alpha Delta Phi Inc. and Chicago Society of Alpha Delta Phi as defendants. “The grief that this has imposed upon me is indescribable,” Doe told NBC News in an interview. “It is the first thing I think about whenever I wake up every day and the last thing I think about whenever I fall asleep.” Doe’s case comes weeks after a former Cornell University student claimed in a lawsuit that she was gang-raped at a fraternity party, causing national outrage, and just days after a woman reported that she was sexually assaulted at a party hosted by a different fraternity near the University of Chicago. The University of Chicago, which does not recognize fraternities as official student organizations, said in a statement that it was “prepared to help the Chicago Police Department” in its investigation. “These allegations are very disturbing to the University community,” said a university spokesperson, Gerald McSwiggan. “The University of Chicago is committed to addressing and preventing incidents of sexual assault.” Alpha Delta Phi’s national team said in a statement that it is aware of the allegations and that it “suspended the member involved.” “The conduct described is deeply troubling and inconsistent with our values,” it said. “We are committed to the safety and well-being of our members and communities and will cooperate with law enforcement as appropriate.” Alpha Delta Phi’s Chicago chapter referred all requests to its national organization. Doe — who is not a student at the University of Chicago — said she learned about the party on Instagram and had gone to parties at the fraternity house previously. That night, she said, she went to the party with several friends, none of whom are students at the university. Doe said she was dancing with friends when a fraternity brother approached her. The fraternity brother offered her a shot, which she said immediately made her feel unsteady and lightheaded, according to the lawsuit. She said she had had only two drinks before she took the shot, spaced out over roughly two hours. She described having the “spins” and feeling as though her “vision was underwater.” “I know myself, and that was not the amount with how intoxicated I felt after the shot that I took with him,” she said. “I’ve never felt like that before.” She added that she watched the fraternity brother pour the shot and did not notice anything “odd.” The fraternity member then directed Doe to follow him to a secluded bedroom on a different floor of the fraternity house, according to the lawsuit. Doe expressed her unsteadiness and lightheadedness, which the fraternity member ignored, the lawsuit says. The fraternity brother began to make “unwanted and nonconsensual sexual advances” on the woman, the lawsuit says. It says she “lost all physical and verbal ability to refuse” the fraternity member’s alleged sexual advances. “I remember backing onto the bed because I knew what was about to happen, but I just — I didn’t feel like I was strong enough to get out,” she told NBC News. The lawsuit says that although her verbal ability was limited, she managed to plead with the fraternity brother to wear a condom, which he refused to do. The fraternity brother then penetrated her “without her consent,” the lawsuit says. After the alleged encounter, the man left Doe alone and unconscious, according to the suit. It alleges that other fraternity brothers initially blocked her friend from going upstairs to find her. Her friend found her unconscious and helped her out of the house, according to the complaint. She said that she faintly remembers her shirt being on backward when she woke up but that she was not sure how she got her clothes on. She struggled to speak and walk as they escorted her out of the home, according to the lawsuit. Doe said she slept over at her friend’s dorm room that night. The next morning, Doe found bloodstains in her underwear and went to the hospital, where she reported the incident to the Chicago Police Department, according to a police report. Doe told police she believed the alcohol was laced with something, according to the report. Police confirmed that a 19-year-old who reported a sexual assault at the fraternity house took herself to Illinois Masonic Hospital for treatment on Feb. 8. Doe received a sexual assault evidence collection kit at the hospital, according to the police report. Days later, the woman was contacted by the University of Chicago Police Department, which she said was investigating her case. Doe said that university police spoke with her for roughly 30 minutes over the phone but that she has not heard from them since. The university police department declined to give Doe records related to her case without a subpoena, she alleges in her lawsuit. A spokesperson for the city’s police department said it was investigating the incident; the spokesperson did not answer questions about the university police department’s involvement in the case. Doe is seeking a trial by jury and an amount in excess of $200,000, plus costs. Doe’s lawyer, Mike Grieco of Gould Grieco & Hensley, said the aim is to also “ensure that this doesn’t happen again, and to help reform” policies within the university. The University of Chicago has been roiled in recent days by a separate allegation of a sexual assault at a fraternity party near campus. A 21-year-old woman told police she was sexually assaulted this month at a party held at the Alpha Epsilon Pi fraternity house, just off campus. Chicago police said no arrests have been made in either case. “At the end of the day, what happened to me is not unique, and it’s not rare. It happens way more than people realize,” Doe said. “There are so many other survivors out there who suffer in silence.”

articles.title: Vacation spot slapped with US travel warning over crime, sexual assaults and kidnappings
articles.summary: Citing violent crime, kidnapping, terrorism and health risks across the popular safari destination, the U.S. State Department raised Kenya's travel advisory to Level 3.
articles.body: The U.S. State Department has escalated its travel warning for an East African nation popular for its wildlife safaris, urging Americans to reconsider visiting amid heightened health concerns and ongoing security threats. The State Department on Monday raised its travel advisory for Kenya from Level 2, "Exercise Increased Caution," to Level 3, "Reconsider Travel." Health risks and crime were cited among the reasons for the advisory, along with civil unrest, kidnapping, terrorism and traffic safety concerns. AMERICANS WARNED OF KIDNAPPING, EXTORTION AS VIOLENT CRIME GRIPS PARTS OF TOURIST SPOT "Prepare a will," the advisory added. "Establish a proof of life protocol with your loved ones." Americans are urged to avoid certain neighborhoods in Nairobi and several counties across the country due to risks of crime, kidnapping and terrorism — as well as areas near the Ethiopian border due to unrest. In its broader warning about the country, State Department officials said that violent crime "can occur at any time," noting that petty crime "is common" throughout Kenya. The advisory also noted that solo travelers should exercise caution, and that some Americans have been sexually assaulted in bars, resorts and hotels. "Local police often are unable to respond effectively to crimes," the advisory said. SEXUAL ASSAULTS AND SCAMS PLAGUE TOP VACATION HOT SPOT, PROMPTING URGENT ADVISORY The State Department also warned that Americans frequently fall victim to investment scams involving gold and other high-value commodities, with Kenyan authorities unlikely to help victims recover their losses. "Property disputes are common in Kenya," added the warning. "Americans who have bought land, churches and businesses have lost their investments or been pushed off the property by locals who claim the land or business." Medical services in Kenya are limited, particularly in rural areas, with some facilities lacking essential medicines and equipment. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "Except for a few private medical facilities based in the large urban centers with enhanced capability, many health issues may require medical evacuation at your own expense," officials said. "Medical facilities will usually deny service if payment is not made upfront." The advisory also warned that protests can turn violent — with demonstrators previously attacking vehicles carrying Americans, including safari vehicles and motorcycle taxis. Americans are urged to stay alert in tourist spots, keep a low profile and avoid demonstrations and crowds while visiting the country. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Kenya is known around the world for its wildlife safaris, picturesque savannas and national parks, which all draw millions of international tourists each year. The country attracted approximately 2.7 million international visitors in 2025, with travelers from the Americas accounting for 14% of arrivals, according to government tourism figures. Last month, the State Department updated its travel advisory for Peru, warning Americans about crime, civil unrest, kidnapping and terrorism. articles.title: Houthis attack besieged city in Yemen that U.N. says is at ‘grave risk’
articles.summary: The Houthis have largely encircled Taiz, cutting it off from most supply routes and putting civilians at “grave risk,” U.N. human rights chief Volker Türk said.
articles.body: TAIZ, Yemen — Iran-backed Houthi rebels struck a residential area in Yemen’s third-largest city Tuesday, killing two teenage girls and renewing attention on the dangers faced by civilians in Taiz, which has been under attack and siege during the country’s escalating conflict. The Houthis have largely encircled Taiz, cutting it off from most supply routes and putting civilians at “grave risk,” U.N. human rights chief Volker Türk said Tuesday. The U.N. says the siege of the strategically important city in southwestern Yemen has left many residents without food and other necessities as prices soar. The attack on Taiz came a day after a Houthi strike on a government military camp killed 73 recruits, the deadliest strike since the resurgence of the conflict over the summer, according to a senior Yemeni government official. The conflict has intensified since forces from the internationally recognized government and Saudi-led coalition launched airstrikes on Houthi-held Sanaa International Airport in July, shattering a 2022 ceasefire deal that largely stopped fighting in the country’s civil war. Yemen has become a widening front in the Iran war that began in February — and the Houthis have increasingly launched attacks on Saudi Arabia because it supports Yemen’s internationally recognized government. Britain said Tuesday that it would expand its military support for Saudi Arabia to include “defensive” air patrols by Royal Air Force jets. U.N. says Houthi siege of Taiz risks humanitarian crisis Heavy fighting between the Houthis and Yemeni government forces caused extensive damage in a densely populated residential area of Taiz. Six people were wounded in the Houthis’ deadly attack there. Resident Zainab Ali said she was away when the strike occurred but returned to find her home had been destroyed. “We are a family of orphans, and we do not know what to do,” she said. Late Tuesday, Yemen’s government forces claimed — without providing evidence — that they had thwarted Houthi attacks in several areas across Taiz and had killed dozens of Houthi fighters. The claim could not be independently verified, and the Houthis did not immediately comment. The rebel group rarely releases its own casualty figures. A strategic gateway to southern Yemen, Taiz has been a focal point of fighting since the civil war began more than a decade ago; it is also one of Yemen’s most important historic and cultural centers. Houthi fighters began advancing again on Taiz last month, after capturing the port city of Mokha, an area vital to controlling shipping through the Red Sea. The Houthis have besieged Taiz as part of their monthslong offensive, repeatedly targeting Yemeni government forces with missiles and artillery. “Humanitarian aid must be immediately allowed to enter the city and its passage must be facilitated. Civilians wishing to leave must be allowed to do so freely and safely,” Türk, the U.N. human rights chief, said. He urged the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces to avoid using explosive weapons in areas where they could hit civilians and civilian infrastructure. Britain pledges additional support to defend Saudi Arabia While Saudi Arabia said Tuesday that it intercepted a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis, the country has struggled to defend against the rebel group’s missile and drone attacks despite far superior U.S.-supplied arms. “Saudi Arabia is in a very difficult position,” but the United States is not prepared to send troops to help, Tom Barrack, the U.S. envoy to Syria and Iraq, told the Global Security Forum in Doha, Qatar. Barrack said President Donald Trump “has been clear that he supports Saudi Arabia, and the backing that they need logistically we’ll supply, but America getting involved in a ground kinetic battle somewhere else seems fruitless.” U.K. Defense Secretary Wes Streeting said the British government would expand its support to Saudi Arabia to include defensive patrols to protect Saudi cities from attacks. It means British planes would attack missiles or drones in the air, but would not strike Houthi targets on the ground. Britain had already offered to help with in-air refueling of Saudi planes. The Egyptian government also will deploy air defense systems and aircraft to help repel missiles and drones fired toward Saudi Arabia but won’t deploy ground troops to Yemen, according to a regional official who was briefed on the matter. The official spoke on condition of anonymity because he wasn’t authorized to speak to reporters. The matter still requires parliamentary approval. Houthis attacked a Yemeni military camp as recruits were being trained The Monday strike on the al-Alam military camp hit while recruits were lining up in formation for a training session. More than 200 recruits were wounded in the attack. Videos from the area circulated online and analyzed by The Associated Press showed many motionless bodies lying on the sandy ground of the camp. The recruits were all aged between 18 and 20, Shabwa governor Awad Ibn al-Wazir told AP. They were being trained to provide security in the province and not for combat operations, he said. Yemen plunged into civil war in 2014, when the Houthis seized Sanaa and much of northern Yemen and forced the government into exile. A Saudi-led coalition intervened the following year in an attempt to restore the government to power. The conflict killed more than 150,000 people and created one of the world’s worst humanitarian disasters.

articles.title: In 2016, a couple paid $1.05 million for a 1923 Hollywood villa built by Rudolph Valentino for Pola Negri; after restoring its historic details, they have sold it for $2.5 million
articles.summary: The old Hollywood home at 6823 Iris Circle in Los Angeles has sold for $2.5 million, fetching $205,000 above its asking price, according to Mansion Global.
articles.body: The old Hollywood home at 6823 Iris Circle in Los Angeles has sold for $2.5 million, fetching $205,000 above its asking price, according to Mansion Global. The price is a strong result for a 1923 Spanish Revival house that its owners restored after buying it for $1.05 million in 2016. The hillside home in Whitley Heights is believed to have been commissioned by Rudolph Valentino for his paramour, stage and screen actress Pola Negri, according to local lore cited by Robb Report.The sellers listed the house in early July for $2.295 million. Two weeks later, a buyer had the property under contract, and the sale closed in July. Greg Shenon of Equity Union represented the buyers.The sellers bought the house for $1.05 millionJames Roncal and Stuart Marks bought the house in 2016. They paid $1.05 million for the property, according to PropertyShark records. “We fell in love with the grounds, the style of the house and the neighbourhood, and we knew we could do a very cool resto-reno to bring our own style to the house while respecting its history and tradition,” the sellers previously told the outlet.After buying the historic house, they decided to renovate it. They wanted to preserve some of its historic elements while incorporating modern features to suit their tastes. They redesigned the kitchen with a mid-century feel. They also updated both bathrooms and two of the three fireplaces, leaving the third untouched. The primary bedroom still has its original Batchelder tiles, an Arts and Crafts feature prized by collectors. The 2,500-square-foot property also includes a two-bedroom main house. A casita dating from 1930 sits on the grounds, with its own bedroom, bathroom, living room, kitchen and patio.A love affairThe Killian house was built in 1923 by Arthur S. Barnes, according to the listing by Plus Real Estate. The American architect worked in Los Angeles from around 1918 to 1928 and designed homes in Spanish, Italian and Mediterranean styles. The Killian house is often linked to Rudolph Valentino and Pola Negri. Local lore suggests that Valentino had it built for Negri, his lover, who was one of the biggest silent film stars of her day. Negri's name appeared in gossip columns for years, mostly because of her romances with Charlie Chaplin and Valentino. After Valentino died in 1926, Negri made headlines at his funeral. She fainted more than once and left a flower arrangement by his casket that read ‘Pola’. However, there is no documented evidence linking Valentino to the house or suggesting that he commissioned it.Inside the homeThe 1920s house retains its original character while making room for modern comforts. It has three bedrooms and three bathrooms, according to the listing. The primary bedroom has its own wood-burning fireplace, a bathroom with a calm, spa-like feel, and a large picture window that frames the greenery. A second bedroom opens onto the garden, and a full guest bathroom is on the main floor.The living room has arched windows, a wood-burning fireplace and French doors that open onto the garden. Upstairs, an office and viewing tower lead to a deck with views of the hills and the Hollywood Sign. Original hardwood floors, detailed ironwork, casement windows and Batchelder tiles feature throughout the house. The restored details sit alongside modern updates. The kitchen features custom walnut cabinets, black quartz worktops, and Wolf and Sub-Zero appliances. The nearby dining room looks out over the treetops.A famous neighbourhoodThe Spanish Revival home stands in Los Angeles's Whitley Heights neighbourhood. The area was developed early in the 20th century by H.J. Whitley, who wanted a hillside village with a Mediterranean feel. Charlie Chaplin, Bette Davis and Gloria Swanson all lived there at one point, making it one of the first celebrity neighbourhoods in the city.Today, it is one of the most architecturally intact historic districts in Los Angeles, protected by its National Register listing and a city preservation overlay. That protection is a major reason buyers pay a premium here. The property cannot simply be demolished and replaced with a new building.Todd Bachenheimer of Modern California House, who co-listed the home with Matt Schwartz of Plus Real Estate, said buyers keep coming back to authenticity and timeless design. “This meticulously restored Spanish Revival home perfectly captures a sense of romance and classic Hollywood glamour,” the listing says. The sale suggests that buyers agree.Although the listing agents did not disclose any information about the buyer, they confirmed that the new owner appreciates the house's details. “My clients were immediately drawn to the home’s exceptional restoration, architectural integrity, and the rarity of finding a property that so successfully blends historic character with modern liveability,” Shenon said.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision?
